Jeffreys Prior on a Block of Coefficients

Source: R/jeffreys.R
jfp.Rd

Specifies a block of coefficients under the prior \(|\tilde I(\beta)|^{a}\), where \(\tilde I\) is the expected Fisher information of the block's coefficients. With \(a = 1/2\) this is the Jeffreys prior on the block, and over every coefficient of a binomial regression it is the penalty of Firth (1993).

Usage

jfp(x, label = "jfp", power = 0.5, intercept = NULL, sparse = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A one-sided formula, such as ~ x1 + x2 or ~ 0 + g, or a numeric matrix, ideally a matrix column of the model data frame. A two-sided formula is rejected with an error.

label

A single non-empty character string prefixed to the coefficient names as label.name, "jfp" by default.

power

The power \(a\) of the determinant, a single positive number; 0.5 by default.

intercept

NULL (the default), TRUE or FALSE: whether the constant direction of the formula level enters the determinant, by the rule above.

sparse

Governs the formula route: TRUE builds a dgCMatrix through Matrix::sparse.model.matrix(), FALSE a dense model matrix, and NULL, the default, settles it at build from the size of the design. A matrix input needs no such argument. See the section above.

...

Not used. Any argument supplied here is rejected with an error that names it and lists the penalty's hyperparameters. The typical case is an argument named after another penalty's hyperparameter: scad(~ x, gamma = 1) signals "'scad' has no argument 'gamma'.".

Value

An unbuilt JeffreysTerm(). The build attaches a JeffreysPenalty() over the block's columns.

Details

The penalty added to the negative log-likelihood is $$\rho(\beta) = -a\log|\tilde I(\beta)|,\qquad \tilde I = \sum_t w_t\sum_{q,r}\mathcal I_{qr}(\eta_t)\, \tilde v_{q,t}^\top\tilde v_{r,t},$$ with \(\mathcal I_{qr}\) the expected information of the family on the link scale and \(\tilde v_{q,t}\) the derivative of the predictor of equation \(q\) with respect to the block's coefficients, preceded by the constant direction when it is included. It depends on the family and on every predictor of the model, and the fitting layer evaluates it together with its derivatives.

The power is fixed. There is no hyperparameter, so nothing is estimated for this term and it adds no row to an outer criterion.

The constant direction of a formula level is the derivative of the predictor along a constant shift of that level's linear predictor: the column of ones for an equation. With intercept = NULL it is included when the column of ones lies in the span of the level's unpenalized columns and not in the span of the block, so the penalty is invariant to centering a column of the block whenever the model is. TRUE includes it unless the block already spans the column of ones, and FALSE never includes it.

The penalty moves an estimate as \(a\,\tilde p\) pseudo-observations would, with \(\tilde p\) the size of \(\tilde I\): with a Poisson log link and an intercept in the model, \(\sum_t(\hat\mu_t - y_t) = a\tilde p\). On a dispersion or shape parameter the effect is strong: the degrees of freedom of a Student t fitted to Gaussian data stay finite.

A formula is coded with its contrasts, as linpar() codes it, and the intercept column is then removed, so jfp(~ g) over a factor of \(k\) levels gives the \(k - 1\) contrasts and jfp(~ 0 + g) all \(k\) indicators. This differs from ridge(), whose formula gives every indicator: the Jeffreys penalty depends on the predictor alone, so it does not identify the direction in which a full set of indicators and the equation's intercept trade a constant. A block whose columns are linearly dependent is rejected when the term is built.

References

Firth, D. (1993). Bias reduction of maximum likelihood estimates. Biometrika 80, 27–38.

Kosmidis, I. and Firth, D. (2021). Jeffreys-prior penalty, finiteness and shrinkage in binomial-response generalized linear models. Biometrika 108, 71–82.

See also

JeffreysPenalty(), ridge() for the same input handling.

Examples

set.seed(3)
dd <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(20), x2 = rnorm(20))
b <- term_build(jfp(~ x1 + x2), dd)
b@coef_names
#> [1] "jfp.x1" "jfp.x2"
b@penalty@power
#> [1] 0.5

# one entry, with no hyperparameter
e <- term_penalties(b)
e[[1]]$penalty@params
#> character(0)
